name: skills
description: The skills system itself: discover more skills, load them well, author your own. Load when you need capabilities you don't currently have.

content.inline:
## Skills
Your [Skills] index lists what your configured sources offer. Beyond it:

Discover:
- The skills op: `{command: "list", sources?}` renders an index over ANY sources — other workspace directories, a shared asset, another user's published set. `{command: "read", name?|ref?}` shows one skill in full without loading it.
- Skills are assets: anyone can hand you one as an `a/<hash>` ref.

Load well:
- skill_load `{name}` from your index, or `{ref}` for any address. Instructions arrive in the result immediately and stay in context each turn; the skill's tools join your palette from your next step.
- Unload with context_unload on the skill's path when done — loaded skills consume budget every turn. The Context Map shows what you carry.
- Loading is idempotent by content: the same skill from two addresses loads once.
- A tool you need without its skill? You can call any operation directly by its catalog path or asset ref as the tool name — dispatch resolves references (capability-gated as usual).

Author (for yourself or other agents):
- A skill is asset metadata: `{name, description, content: {inline: "...markdown..."}, skill: {tools: ["v/ops/..."]}}`. Write it to `w/skills/<name>` (covia write) for personal use — your `w/skills` shadows same-named venue skills — or store as an asset (asset store) to share. SKILL.md-style frontmatter in content is also understood.
- description = ONE line saying what it does and when to load it; body = tight instructions + gotchas; tools = full catalog paths. Contentless skill = pure toolset.
